title: Fragment Fusion PRD sandbox
summary: Rough sketch for a lightweight feature that composes short conversational fragments (snippets) into cohesive responses with cost-aware fallbacks and UX affordances for developers.
body:
Context and motivation:
- Observed pattern: many product flows want short, high-precision snippets (facts, inventory hits, clarifying questions) stitched into a final assistant reply.
- Current approaches: single long generation (expensive, brittle), or naive concatenation of multiple model calls (latency/cost spike, ordering issues).
- Opportunity: treat fragments as first-class micro-responses with a small composition layer (ordering heuristics, templating, cheap join models) to reduce cost and improve control.

Idea (one-liner):
- Allow the application to request N small fragments (varying model sizes/qualty) and a lightweight composer operation that merges them into a single output. Composer can be local deterministic code + optional small LM for surface fluency.

Key pillars:
1) Fragment types: fact, clarification, option-list, cite, micro-summary.
2) Cost laddering: fragments can be fetched from cheaper models or cache and only escalate for uncertain fragments.
3) Composer modes: deterministic template join; templated LM polish (small 2-4B); preserve provenance tokens for traceability.
4) Fallback policy: if fragments are missing or low-confidence, composer uses best-effort synthesis or returns partial output with explicit markers.

Sketch flow (developer view):
1) Client sends a combine request: prompt template includes slots for fragments and composition mode.
2) Server-side orchestration issues parallel fragment calls with per-fragment model hints.
3) Fragments return with confidence signals (logprobs, eval hooks).
4) Composer merges fragments: (a) deterministic merge if mode=structured; (b) run small-lm polish if mode=fluent.
5) Final response streamed back with fragment metadata in headers or a companion stream.

Why this helps:
- Cost: using targeted smaller calls + composer reduces average tokens consumed by main model and avoids re-generating overlapping context.
- Latency: parallel fragment calls can be bounded and composer is cheap; critical path sometimes shorter than monolithic generation.
- Debuggability: per-fragment telemetry simplifies failure modes and A/B testing.
- Product flexibility: teams can mix-and-match fragment types and composer modes per route.

ML/infra considerations:
- KV caching of repeated fragments (e.g., static facts, product snippets).
- Router heuristics for per-fragment model selection (based on route, token budget, past quality).
- Composer must be reproducible across Dedicated/Private installs: deterministic fallback algorithm + small polish model optional.
- Instrumentation: token-level costing per fragment, latency histogram, confidence vs. quality signals.

Minimal viable scope (alpha):
- Support 3 fragment types: fact, option-list, micro-summary.
- Server orchestration + deterministic composer only (no polish LM).
- Developer API: add fragments array and composer.mode field.
- Telemetry: per-fragment tokens, simple confidence flag, compose latencies.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I can request up to 5 fragments and a deterministic composer to stitch them into a single assistant reply so I can keep usage predictable.
- As a data engineer, I want fragment-level telemetry so I can correlate fragment confidence with downstream user satisfaction.
- As an SRE, I want composer to run on CPU-only fallback so Private customers without GPUs still get basic functionality.

Success metrics (initial):
- 20% reduction in median token spend for targeted routes compared to monolithic gen.
- No more than +10% p50 latency for routes that use fragments (goal: reduce p95).
- Fewer than 5% user-visible composition failures in alpha (composition failure = missing fragments + unable to provide partial).

Open questions / risks:
- Ordering and coherence: how to guarantee fragment ordering matches conversation pragmatics? (heuristics vs. small reorderer LM)
- Privacy/provenance: how to surface fragment origins without leaking internal IDs or too much metadata?
- QA: how do we generate training sets to evaluate composer quality? Need curated prompt+fragment pairs.
- UX: Do devs want fragments exposed or prefer abstracted blocks with types?

Implementation TODOs (next steps):
- Spike: prototype composer as a small deterministic joiner + optional 2B polish; bench cost/latency in hosted env. (ENG ticket JIRA-ENG-1428)
- Design: draft API surface (fragments[], composer.mode, per-fragment hints) and SDK ergonomics.
- Telemetry: define events and tags for fragment lifecycle; wire basic dashboards.
- Security review: ensure fragment metadata doesn't leak.

Notes to self / quick decisions:
- Keep deterministic composer first to minimize infra lift.
- For alpha, limit per-fragment token limit to 150 tokens to cap worst-case.
- Expose fragment confidence as a numeric 0-1 and a simple quality enum: {ok, low, unknown}.

References / Related work:
- See convo-slice experiments (link in linked_artifacts) for prior partitioning heuristics.
- Look at microresponse profiles and the session-surface cuebook for UX patterns.

Rough API sketch (developer facing) - informal:
POST /v1/responses
{
  "input": "User message...",
  "fragments": [
    {"id":"product-facts","type":"fact","hint":"small-model"},
    {"id":"clarifier","type":"clarification","hint":"cheap-if-certain"}
  ],
  "composer": {"mode":"deterministic", "template":"{{facts}}\nOptions:\n{{options}}"}
}

Response contains: final_text, fragments_meta[] (id, model, tokens, confidence), compose_time_ms

----
Random brain-dump ideas to try later:
- Adaptive fragment deadlines: if a slow fragment misses deadline, use cached value or mark placeholder.
- Fragment prefetching on route hits (cache warmers).
- Developer tool: fragment inspector in Console that replays fragment calls and allows toggle of polish LM.

End of draft.
user_stories: Product engineer: request multiple fragments with deterministic composition to reduce cost and control output
SRE: composer can degrade to CPU-only deterministic mode for Private customers
Observability owner: gets per-fragment metrics to correlate with downstream success
success_metrics: 20% median token reduction for pilot routes
<=10% p50 latency increase for fragmentized routes
